Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — private VPC dataflow and privacy questions

Thanks again for the call earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of requirements we heard:
- AcmeHealth will be routing PHI-containing request payloads to Redwood inference for feature X.
- Must support Private VPC deployment with no public egress for request payloads (customer-initiated egress only).
- Data residency: production inference must remain in us-east-1; backup metrics may be stored in an encrypted S3 bucket in the same region.
- Retention: request/response logs to be retained for 90 days for troubleshooting; aggregated usage metrics only thereafter unless flagged for investigation.
- Audit & logging: need tamper-evident audit logs, per-request tracing IDs, and KMS-backed envelope encryption.
- On-prem requirement: evaluation of an air-gapped option for a locked-down staging environment (no outward internet).

Attachments included: redwood-private-vpc-dataflow-diagram.png, redwood-privacy-qna.docx (detailed answers to the initial questionnaire).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical design review — 60min session with your infra/security + our infra engineers (I recommend including Dev Patel and Evelyn Hart).
2) Share a short dataflow diagram we can iterate on (attached).
3) Follow up with our SOC/compliance pack and KMS/HSM integration notes (we've attached the privacy Q&A).
4) If that looks good, we can schedule a pilot Private deployment into a dedicated VPC (timeline dependent on legal/contract).

Are you available for a design review on Tue 6/30 10:00–11:00 AM ET or Wed 7/1 2:00–3:00 PM ET? I can send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Thanks,

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few follow-ups from our side after reviewing the attachments: 

1) Retention & PII handling:
- Confirm that we can configure token-level redaction for any fields we mark as sensitive before logs are persisted.
- We prefer a default 30-day retention for raw request/response logs and a 365-day retention for aggregated metrics unless otherwise negotiated — can you confirm what is configurable?

2) Audit logs / tamper-evidence:
- Can you describe the auditing chain-of-custody? We need proof that logs cannot be altered without detection and timestamps are immutable.

3) KMS/HSM integration:
- We use a customer-managed KMS in AWS (AWS KMS with a CMK). Is that supported for envelope encryption, and can we rotate keys on our schedule?

4) On-prem / air-gapped option:
- For our regulated staging environment we need zero outbound connections to public internet. Is there an offline installer or an air-gapped deployment model you support? If not, what mitigations exist?

5) Network boundaries and egress controls:
- Need confirmation that inference-serving nodes will not initiate outbound traffic except to customer-managed artifact storage (if configured).

Can we also get a brief writeup for our legal team on data flows and third parties? I've attached our compliance requirements summary (acme_health_compliance_requirements.pdf).

If the proposed times work, let's lock in Tue 6/30 10:00–11:00 AM ET — Alice and I can attend.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — private VPC dataflow and privacy questions

Thanks Bob — great questions. Quick answers up-front, and we'll deep-dive during the design call tomorrow.

1) Retention & PII redaction:
- Yes — retention windows are configurable per-customer and per-environment. We can set raw request/response logs to 30 days and aggregated metrics to 365 days by policy.
- Token/field redaction: we support configurable preprocessors that redact or hash fields you mark as PII before logs touch persistent storage. We can include sample preprocessor rules in the follow-up doc.

2) Audit logs / tamper-evidence:
- Audit logs are written to an append-only store with write-once configuration. We support signed log entries using per-host signing keys and can export a signed audit bundle for compliance review. We'll share the SOC2/compliance pack in the follow-up.

3) KMS/HSM integration:
- Customer-managed AWS KMS keys (CMKs) are supported for envelope encryption. Key rotation on your schedule is supported; the runtime accepts CMKs for decrypting per-session keys. For HSM-backed keys, we integrate with AWS CloudHSM via CMK if required.

4) On-prem / air-gapped:
- We do offer an on-prem package for air-gapped evaluations. It requires an initial import of signed artifacts and an offline license handshake. No outbound internet is required; we can run entirely within your network boundary. We'll have Dev walk through the requirements and the offline installer flow on the call.

5) Network boundaries & egress:
- Serving nodes do not initiate outbound connections by default. Any outbound (e.g., object storage, metrics export) is configurable and can be restricted to customer-managed endpoints only. We support VPC endpoints and private link-like configs to avoid public egress.

Call: confirming Tue 6/30 10:00–11:00 AM ET for the design review — I've sent a calendar invite. Agenda will be: dataflow walkthrough (15m), network/egress controls & KMS (20m), retention & redaction configuration (15m), next steps & pilot plan (10m).

See you tomorrow — attaching a short checklist for what we'll need from your side.

Thanks,

Hi Bob / Alice — Dev from the Redwood infra team here. Wanted to add some technical notes ahead of the call and a quick description of the air-gapped/on-prem flow so you can share with your security team: 

Network boundaries:
- In the Private deployment, all inference nodes live in your VPC or in a customer-dedicated subnet we deploy into your cloud account. We do not create public IPs.
- All control-plane communication can be routed through a private control channel (customer-managed endpoint).

Egress controls:
- No outbound internet by default. Object storage exports, monitoring, or metrics exports only talk to endpoints you configure (S3 buckets, Datadog ingest endpoints, etc.).
- We support NAT-less deployments; if you require zero egress we provide an offline artifact bundle and an operator-run install (air-gapped).

Data-at-rest & encryption:
- Data at rest is encrypted with customer CMKs (AWS KMS) or local HSM-protected keys for on-prem installs. Key material never leaves your key manager; we perform envelope encryption using per-session keys.

Audit & logs:
- Application logs are stream-signed and written to append-only storage. For highest assurance, we can configure a write-once S3 bucket with object lock (governance mode) and provide signed manifests daily.

Operational constraints for air-gapped staging:
- Offline installer package (signed) + offline license file.
- Operator must import container images or pre-pulled artifacts via a secure transfer.
- No automatic updates; all patches are manual, signed updates.

I'll bring a proposed network diagram (private-vpc-dataflow-v1.drawio) to the call and can walk through the offline installer steps. Happy to answer any specific questions during the session.

Thanks,
